title: CULTURESCORE: Evaluating Cultural Faithfulness in Video Generation Models

bias_targets.methodology: The paper introduces CULTURESCORE, a framework that evaluates cultural faithfulness by decomposing prompts into three grounded facets: Identity (demographic markers, attire), Behavior (normative gestures), and Context (localized backgrounds). It uses Vision-Language Models (VLMs) and native human evaluators to score model outputs across 10 countries and 5 socio-cultural domains.

The study employs 'Geographical Constraint Removed' prompts to determine if models rely on explicit geographic identifiers (e.g., 'Indian') or have internalized cultural knowledge as geography-independent representations, comparing performance across 10 specific nations.

The evaluation benchmark includes a specific 'Religion' domain to assess the accurate depiction of spiritual frameworks, rituals, and associated visual markers, such as Islamic calligraphy, Persian rugs, and traditional attire (e.g., white kurta).
